text:
ameya: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing we extract a small 'runtime-sheen' adapter as a first-class service to own cross-cutting transform/compat logic. Goal: small surface, high-safety cutover. Thoughts?

jordan: TL;DR what does runtime-sheen actually own vs the existing request-router?

ameya: Sheen would sit between the router and model runtimes. Responsibilities: 1) light canonicalization of inputs (timestamp formats, legacy fields), 2) policy-driven response shaping (truncate, map headers), 3) backwards-compatible shims for older model variants. Not responsible for routing/affinity or auth/quotas.

lia: Sounds useful. Main risk is splitting auth/tenant checks 02014 we should keep auth upstream in the router. Can sheen call the auth service? Latency concerns if networked.

sam: +1 to keeping auth upstream. Also: how do we avoid doubling per-request latency by inserting an extra RPC hop?

ameya: Plan: start as an in-process module for hotpath workers behind a feature flag, then migrate to a networked service when perf budget allows. That lets us iterate without immediate perf tax.

jordan: Could we do a single binary with a pluggable sheen interface first? Preserves deployment simplicity but still gives ownership boundaries.

lia: We did something similar for the encrypter sidecar. In-process + flag worked well for rollout; ops preferred no immediate extra pod.

sam: Ops note: if sheen is in-process we need guardrails for memory growth. Sheen will have small normalization caches; add eviction and memory metrics.

devon: For cutover checkpoints: 1) regression prompt smoke tests, 2) latency baseline vs canary, 3) automatic rollback thresholds (p95 +0.8s OR failure rate +2%). I can own the dashboard and alerts.

ameya: Draft rollout steps (spike -> in-proc flag -> canary region -> global traffic):

# feature flag example
SERVICE_RUNTIME_FLAGS=--sheen=inproc
# sample smoke test
curl -s -X POST https://staging.redwood/api/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'

jordan: Need a compatibility matrix mapping old fields -> new canonical names. Store it in the sheen repo as markdown + unit tests.

lia: Also add a config-driven allowlist for shims (tenant opt-in). Enterprise customers may want to opt out of transformations.

sam: Observability: tag spans/traces when sheen mutates payloads. Otherwise diffs between with/without sheen are hard to reason about.

devon: I'll add a tracing span called 'sheen.transform' and metrics sheen.transform.count with labels {tenant, transform_type}.

ameya: Policy decision: sheen will annotate payloads but will not enforce or alter auth/quotas. That remains the router + policy plane's responsibility.

jordan: Tests: add an e2e harness that runs regression prompts against both paths (with and without sheen) and asserts semantic equivalence within config bounds.

ameya: I'll draft the RFC follow-up doc and compatibility matrix in the repo by EOD. @devon can you create the dashboard and rollback alerts?

devon: On it 02014 will post the dashboard link here when ready.

deploy-bot: Scheduled provisional canary deployment window: 2023-10-04 22:00 UTC (sheen-inproc). Owners must ack 24h before.

lia: Ack.
jordan: Ack.
sam: Ack.
ameya: Thanks team 02014 I'll drop the follow-up RFC + checklist in the repo tonight.
